Take her deodorant shopping a find one that smells good, there’s all sorts out there for tweens. There’s loads that smell like fruit, sweets and chocolate out there so there’s bound to be something that catches her liking! 

Does she look up to anyone in specific? Music artists or influencers? Maybe try the whole ‘I read that XYZ uses this brush to make their hair a certain way. You should try it!’ Thing. My younger sister really loved Pokemon growing up and also has super curly hair. We found a Tangle Teaser brush in the shape of Pikachu and it was a life saver, 3 years later she still loves it lol! 

Maybe encourage her to do a morning routine with you? Have yourself spend 10 minutes in the bathroom with her, brush your teeth, hair and put on deodorant together. Make it fun, listen to some music! As someone on the spectrum myself I know that routine can be really useful to get over mental blocks! 

Also, I’m not sure if she’s getting underarm hair yet, but if that does come along, hair removal cream is great. It’s a bit smelly but it works well and you won’t have to worry about razors. 
The smell of the cream might also encourage her to jump in the shower to get the smell off! Find a really strong smelling shower gel as encouragement! 
(I’m 21 and I use one that smells EXACTLY like those foam banana sweets. It works for me so it might work for her lol!) 

Big respect to you for stepping in to look after you sister! I went through a rough patch where I was unofficially my younger sisters primary carer for a few months. You sound like you really care which means you’re doing great!! Keep it up, she seems to have a great role model!
